dt <- read.csv("EMC.csv", header = TRUE)
head(dt)
##       Date    Close Adj.Close    Volume
## 1 2018/1/1 40.65391  31.77513 434169504
## 2 2018/2/1 36.41176  28.45946 123130681
## 3 2018/3/1 35.70473  27.90685 169056013
## 4 2018/4/1 35.58690  27.81475  91429091
## 5 2018/5/1 34.99771  27.35424 113872895

names(dt)

dim(dt)
## [1] 60  4

#===============================================================================

# Convert the dataset into a time series object
par(mar = c(4, 4, 3, .5))
ts.dt <- ts(dt)
head(ts.dt)
## Time Series:
## Start = 1 
## End = 6 
## Frequency = 1 
##   Date    Close Adj.Close    Volume
## 1    1 40.65391  31.77513 434169504
## 2    5 36.41176  28.45946 123130681
## 3    6 35.70473  27.90685 169056013
## 4    7 35.58690  27.81475  91429091
## 5    8 34.99771  27.35424 113872895
## 6    9 30.63773  23.94648  91725256
EMC.V <- ts(dt$Volume, start = 2018, frequency = 12)
plot(EMC.V, main = "EMC Volume")

# create training and validation of the EMC stock data
EMC.train <- window(EMC.V, end = 2022)
EMC.test <- window(EMC.V, start = 2018)

ses.EMC <- ses(EMC.train)
autoplot(ses.EMC)

EMC.dif <- diff(EMC.train)
autoplot(EMC.dif)

ses.EMC.dif <- ses(EMC.dif)
autoplot(ses.EMC.dif)

EMC.dif.test <- diff(EMC.test)
accuracy(ses.EMC.dif, EMC.dif.test)
##                    ME      RMSE       MAE      MPE     MAPE      MASE
## Training set 39429183 595576284 324796569 149.3359 272.3176 0.5932317
## Test set     23382823 543049484 399583794 107.9371 107.9371 0.7298284
##                      ACF1 Theil's U
## Training set -0.009568157        NA
## Test set     -0.436227749   1.17209
# Identify optimal alpha parameter
alpha <- seq(.01, .99, by = .01)
RMSE <- NA
for(i in seq_along(alpha)) {
  fit <- ses(EMC.dif, alpha = alpha[i])
  RMSE[i] <- accuracy(fit, EMC.dif.test)[2,2]
}

# Convert to a data frame and identify min. alpha value
alpha.fit <- data.frame(alpha, RMSE)
alpha.min <- filter(alpha.fit, RMSE == min(RMSE))

# Plot RMSE vs. alpha
ggplot(alpha.fit, aes(alpha, RMSE)) + geom_line()

# + geom_point(alpha.min, aes(alpha, RMSE), col = "blue")
# Point cannot point out.

# Refit model with alpha = .05
ses.EMC.opt <- ses(EMC.dif, alpha = .05)

# Performance eval
accuracy(ses.EMC.opt, EMC.dif.test)
##                    ME      RMSE       MAE      MPE     MAPE      MASE
## Training set -9665470 607052663 325901444 100.8568 136.8180 0.5952497
## Test set     18503907 542861290 398608011 106.6966 106.6966 0.7280462
##                     ACF1 Theil's U
## Training set -0.01589604        NA
## Test set     -0.43622775  1.160486
# Plotting results
p1 <- autoplot(ses.EMC.opt) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
p2 <- autoplot(EMC.dif.test, main = "Predicted vs. Actuals for the test data set") + autolayer(ses.EMC.opt, alpha = .5)
par(mfrow = c(1,2))
  p1 ; p2

par(mfrow = c(1,1))

holt.EMC <- holt(EMC.train)
autoplot(holt.EMC)

holt.EMC$model
## Holt's method 
## 
## Call:
##  holt(y = EMC.train) 
## 
##   Smoothing parameters:
##     alpha = 0.9668 
##     beta  = 1e-04 
## 
##   Initial states:
##     l = 271019585.8828 
##     b = -10807145.9506 
## 
##   sigma:  614505649
## 
##      AIC     AICc      BIC 
## 2179.687 2181.082 2189.146
accuracy(holt.EMC, EMC.test)
##                     ME      RMSE       MAE       MPE     MAPE      MASE
## Training set  23053579 588889887 317891811 -4.270844 42.65970 0.3307560
## Test set     169868810 386315761 234638209  9.705113 19.74384 0.2441333
##                      ACF1 Theil's U
## Training set  0.009207622        NA
## Test set     -0.219750035 0.9130507
# Identify optimal alpha parameter
beta <- seq(.0001, .5, by = .001)
RMSE <- NA

for (i in seq_along(beta)) {
  fit <- holt(EMC.train, beta = beta[i], h = 100)
  RMSE[i] <- accuracy(fit, EMC.test)[2,2]
}

# Convert to a data frame and idenitify min alpha value
beta.fit <- data.frame(beta, RMSE)
beta.min <- filter(beta.fit, RMSE == min(RMSE))

# Plot RMSE vs. alpha
ggplot(beta.fit, aes(beta, RMSE)) + geom_line()

# + geom_point(data = beta.min, aes(beta, RMSE), size = 2, color = "blue")

# New model with optimal beta
holt.EMC.opt <- holt(EMC.train, beta = 0.05)

# Accuracy of first model
accuracy(holt.EMC, EMC.test)
##                     ME      RMSE       MAE       MPE     MAPE      MASE
## Training set  23053579 588889887 317891811 -4.270844 42.65970 0.3307560
## Test set     169868810 386315761 234638209  9.705113 19.74384 0.2441333
##                      ACF1 Theil's U
## Training set  0.009207622        NA
## Test set     -0.219750035 0.9130507
# Accuracy of new optimal model
accuracy(holt.EMC.opt, EMC.test)
##                     ME      RMSE       MAE       MPE     MAPE      MASE
## Training set  -2556979 601413588 323271990 -2.700537 44.15467 0.3363539
## Test set     272437183 429427695 296496292 22.211255 26.06661 0.3084946
##                     ACF1 Theil's U
## Training set -0.01689285        NA
## Test set     -0.32668301  1.047537
p3 <- autoplot(holt.EMC, main = "Original Holt's Model")
p4 <- autoplot(holt.EMC.opt, main = "Optimal Holt's Model")
par(mfrow = c(1,2))
  p3 ; p4

par(mfrow = c(1,1))

autoplot(decompose(EMC.V))

# Additive
EMC.hw <- ets(EMC.train, model = "AAA")
autoplot(forecast(EMC.hw))

summary(EMC.hw)

## 
## Call:

##

##     gamma = 1e-04 
## 
##   Initial states:

checkresiduals(EMC.hw)

## 
##  Ljung-Box test
## 
## data:  Residuals from ETS(A,A,A)
## Q* = 17.293, df = 3, p-value = 0.0006151
## 
## Model df: 16.   Total lags used: 19
# Forecast the next 5 quarters
EMC.f1 <- forecast(EMC.hw, h = 5)

# Check accuracy
accuracy(EMC.f1, EMC.test)
##                     ME      RMSE       MAE       MPE      MAPE      MASE
## Training set -40866811 532962047 427984153 -15.96238 221.86884 0.4453034

##                    ACF1 Theil's U
## Training set 0.02202907        NA
## Test set     0.13196641  1.455931
# Multiplicative
EMC.hw2 <- ets(EMC.train, model = "MAM")
checkresiduals(EMC.hw2)

##

accuracy(EMC.f1, EMC.test)

accuracy(EMC.f2, EMC.test)

gamma <- seq(0.01, 0.99, 0.01)
RMSE <- NA

for(i in seq_along(gamma)) {
  hw.expo <- ets(EMC.train, model = "AAA", gamma = gamma[i])
  future <- forecast(hw.expo, h = 5)
  RMSE[i] = accuracy(future, EMC.test)[2,2]
}

error <- data.frame(gamma, RMSE)
minimum <- filter(error, RMSE == min(RMSE))
ggplot(error, aes(gamma, RMSE)) + geom_line() + ggtitle("Gamma's impact on forecast errors", subtitle = "Gamma = 0.45 minimizes RMSE")

# + geom_point(data = minimum, color = "blue", size = 2)

# Holt's linear (additive) model
fit1 <- ets(EMC.V, model = "ZAN", alpha = 0.8, beta = 0.2)
pred1 <- forecast(fit1, h = 5)

# Holt's linear (additive) model
fit2 <- ets(EMC.V, model = "ZAN", damped = TRUE, alpha = 0.8, beta = 0.2, phi = 0.85)
pred2 <- forecast(fit2, h = 5)

# Holt's exponential (multiplicative) model
fit3 <- ets(EMC.V, model = "ZMN", alpha = 0.8, beta = 0.2)
pred3 <- forecast(fit3, h = 5)

# Holt's exponential (multiplicative) model damped
fit4 <- ets(EMC.V, model = "ZMN", damped = TRUE, alpha = 0.8, beta = 0.2, phi = 0.85)
pred4 <- forecast(fit4, h = 5)

autoplot(EMC.V) +
  autolayer(pred1$mean, color = "blue") +
  autolayer(pred2$mean, color = "blue", linetype = "dashed") +
  autolayer(pred3$mean, color = "red") +
  autolayer(pred4$mean, color = "red", linetype = "dashed")
